directories.name: State, territory and tribal drinking-water programs
directories.coverage: State/territory drinking-water program and available database links; includes Navajo Nation.
limitations: Wyoming and District of Columbia do not hold primacy; EPA administers it.
EPA implements SDWA on tribal lands except Navajo Nation.
Not a private-well regulator directory or a guarantee every linked database is current.
A state database may have more detail and newer information than federal SDWIS.
directories.implementation: Offer the directory and label the appropriate agency; do not send every complaint to a utility rate commission.

directories.name: State utility commissions
directories.publisher: National Association of Regulatory Utility Commissioners
directories.publisher_type: Official commission association, not a federal regulator
use_for: Utility billing or service disputes within each commission’s authority
directories.coverage: 50 states and District of Columbia, with territory entries and other regulatory organizations.
limitations: NARUC does not adjudicate utility complaints.
A commission may not regulate the resident’s water provider; municipal, county, cooperative and private systems have different rules.
directories.implementation: Use as an agency directory, then verify the provider against that commission’s regulated-company list before selecting a complaint route.

directories.name: Federal civil-rights complaint offices
use_for: Finding the federal agency with a relevant civil-rights program
directories.coverage: Federal agency civil-rights offices and filing links; directs uncertain users to DOJ.
limitations: Some directory agency names and links are older than destination pages; use the current agency’s own submission instructions.
A directory entry does not establish jurisdiction or that discrimination occurred.
directories.implementation: Offer EPA for alleged discrimination by EPA financial-assistance recipients; offer the DOJ directory when the funding agency is unknown.

supported_complaint_routes.name: EPA External Civil Rights Division complaint
supported_complaint_routes.route_type: Signed written complaint submitted by user through email or postal mail
supported_complaint_routes.form_note: The current EPA filing page requires a signed written complaint; it does not link a standard complaint PDF or a complaint web form. A site-generated letter must not be labeled an official EPA form.

required_information.requirement: Provide contact information; telephone and/or email are suggested.
Include the sender’s signature; accepted electronic-signature formats were not specified on the inspected page.
Identify the entity alleged to have discriminated.
Explain the acts and why they involve prohibited discrimination, intimidation or retaliation.
Needed to assess the filing period; use the last alleged discriminatory act.

jurisdiction: Respondent must receive EPA financial assistance.
A person or organization may complain for someone else.
The allegations must concern a civil-rights law EPA enforces.
exclusions_and_limits: A water problem alone does not establish unlawful discrimination.
EPA says it can investigate only entities receiving EPA financial assistance.
EPA’s general External Civil Rights contact web form expressly is not for filing discrimination complaints.
Louisiana has a specific injunction limiting disparate-impact and cumulative-impact enforcement; it is not a blanket exclusion of all Louisiana civil-rights complaints.

deadline.extension: EPA may consider an extension for good cause; do not reject a user automatically or promise an extension.

submit.postal_address: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, Office of Civil Rights and Adjudication, External Civil Rights Division, Mail Code 1201A, 1200 Pennsylvania Avenue NW, Washington, DC 20460

accessibility.note: Current EPA filing page offers free interpretation/translation and disability accommodations. Translated pages can retain older contact details; prefer current English submission details.

receipt.case_number_mechanism: No automatic receipt or case-number mechanism specified on the inspected filing page.
capture_after_real_submission: EPA acknowledgment or case number when received
receipt.do_not_claim: Generating a PDF, opening email or downloading a letter does not mean the complaint was filed.

implementable_flow: Ask short questions covering required information and user-described facts.
Create a reviewable complaint letter with a signature area.
Have the user review/sign and submit through the official route.
Save a copy and let the user attach actual submission evidence.

supported_complaint_routes.name: Florida PSC regulated water/wastewater complaint
supported_complaint_routes.route_type: Official online form with user completion and CAPTCHA
eligibility_gate: Confirm that the exact utility appears in the PSC company selector; county selection alone is not enough.
PSC advises trying to resolve the problem with the company first and allowing it time to correct it.
supported_complaint_routes.jurisdiction: Investor-owned water/wastewater companies within PSC jurisdiction; current 2026 brochure describes 40 counties. Do not hard-code older 38-county lists.
excluded_issue_examples: Municipally owned or county-owned water/wastewater utilities
Water clarity or pressure (brochure points to DEP)
Water lines beyond the point of connection

fields.meaning: Regulated utility selected from the official list
Destination: PSC or company when offered

field_notes: The live public Angular component requires contact and service state even though the visible labels are not starred.
Email is optional but validated as an email if supplied.
Contact/service ZIP inputs use a five-digit mask.
Account number is optional in current client validation.
The official form can copy contact details to service details; the user must check the result.
Current defaults include FL, Delay in Service and PSC; an assistant should not accept these silently for the user.
There is no attachment field in the inspected component. Do not claim that attaching evidence to this site attaches it to the PSC complaint.

submit.destination_choices: PSC; some companies offer direct company delivery. The user must review the actual destination.
submit.captcha: Official page invokes reCAPTCHA; hand off to the user.

receipt.official_help: Official help tells users to save the tracking number after submitting.
receipt.current_component_observation: The current form displays the server response message and clears the form after success; no live submission was attempted.

supported_complaint_routes.privacy: The official form warns that submitted information may be publicly disclosed under Florida public-records law. Tell the user before the official handoff; do not describe the external complaint as private.

fallback.postal_address: Florida Public Service Commission, Office of Consumer Assistance & Outreach, 2540 Shumard Oak Boulevard, Tallahassee, FL 32399-0850

implementable_flow: Collect and review the mapped fields locally.
Provide a copyable field summary and open the official form.
Let the user choose company, destination and complete CAPTCHA/submission.
Prompt for the actual complaint number and receipt afterward.

additional_fallback.purpose: General federal civil-rights intake when an agency is unclear; DOJ may refer or be unable to help.
additional_fallback.verified_fields: Optional name/contact; active-duty servicemember status question is required in current online step 1. Later sections cover main concern, location, personal characteristics, date, description and review.
additional_fallback.receipt: DOJ says successful online submission yields a confirmation number; follow-up should cite that number.
additional_fallback.response_limit: DOJ does not guarantee updates or individual assistance.
additional_fallback.pdf_caution: The official linked PDF and inspected online footer display OMB expiration 2026-08-31, earlier than this check. Do not silently rehost it as an up-to-date autofill form; prefer the agency’s current live page and ask DOJ about current materials if needed.

property_level_inventory.what_is_available: Utilities/primacy agencies maintain inventories; address-level maps and machine-readable availability vary. No nationwide property-level pipe-material lookup was verified in this research.
required_inventory_elements: Lead / galvanized requiring replacement / non-lead / unknown classification
Separate utility/customer portions where ownership is split
Location identifiers for lead and galvanized-requiring-replacement lines
property_level_inventory.public_access_limit: Initial LCRR inventories need not publish an exact street address; a meaningful location identifier can be used. Systems serving more than 50,000 people must post inventories online; smaller systems can provide another public-access method.
property_level_inventory.implementation: Use a verified utility inventory for a confirmed property match. Otherwise offer a record/inspection request. Never infer material from a nearby line, regional prevalence, absence of a hit, or an unknown classification.

national_service_line_counts.name: EPA SDWIS Service Line Inventory
national_service_line_counts.scope: Community and non-transient non-community water systems; voluntarily reported transient systems can also appear.
limitations: Federal figures depend on state/primacy reporting.
Non-lead count reporting is not required until November 1, 2027; some states already report it, so current totals can undercount.
The dashboard is dynamic. The fresh text-only response showed zero placeholders before a period/data load; do not turn these into zero-line assertions.
No stable documented public bulk/API endpoint for these inventory counts was verified here.
national_service_line_counts.implementable_now: Link the official inventory dashboard and ask the user to select their confirmed system. A future adapter needs a separately validated data export/API and reporting-period handling.
national_service_line_counts.public_label: Reported pipe counts for this water system — not the material at your home.

national_service_area_match.name: EPA Public Water System Service Areas, Version 3
national_service_area_match.coverage_statement: EPA describes more than 44,000 community systems, about 99% of their reported served population, and about 80,000 non-community service areas (roughly 84% of active non-community systems). This is not 99% address-level pipe coverage.
limitations: Boundaries can be modeled estimates or system/state sourced and can contain errors.
A blank verification field is not verification.
An area can contain private wells or another unmapped system.
Many tribal and territorial systems remain unmapped; EPA’s current page says non-community coverage excludes Guam.
Boundaries derived from a lead-service-line inventory remain service-area polygons; they do not disclose this home’s pipe material.
Keep multiple intersecting candidates and seek provider confirmation; do not silently choose a nearby or first result.

verified_read_only_example.purpose: Public Denver city-center point; no user address

national_service_area_match.implementable_now: Query the public layer to suggest candidate providers. Show source/type and ask the resident to confirm using a bill, landlord or utility before joining regulatory or inventory records.

implementation_boundaries: These are preparation and official-handoff routes, not proof of a filed complaint.
Only use user-provided facts; do not infer a protected characteristic, discrimination finding, funding eligibility or legal violation.
Store a draft, actual submission and official acknowledgment as distinct events.
Recheck agency contacts, forms and deadlines before refreshing or publishing a route.
No account was created, CAPTCHA bypassed, complaint submitted, email sent, or external data changed during this research.
